amendments.rule: Carry a case preposition: `τοῦ πληρώματος` → *of the fulness*. Then *of* and *the* form one unit headed on *the*, and the noun stands alone. The English *the* is what anchors that unit, so where the ASV gives the noun no determiner the article carries nothing: it is `unrepresented` under rule 23 and the case preposition stays with the noun. `τῇ προσευχῇ` → *by prayer*, `τῆς εἰρήνης` → *of peace*, `τῷ θεῷ` → *to God*, `τοῖς ἀνθρώποις` → *unto men* are all one unit on the noun. Do not read this rule as licensing a bare *of* or *by* on the article; a determinerless English phrase is rule 23's case, not this one. This rule speaks throughout of a preposition realizing the governed word's **own case**, and an English preposition licensed by something else does not move to that word merely because it stands in front of it. Where the ASV builds a support-verb frame around the Greek verb and the frame's own supplied noun is what licenses the preposition, the preposition belongs to the frame and stays inside the verb's unit, the governed word keeping a bare noun: `οὐ λογίζεται τὸ κακόν` → *taketh not account of evil* gives *taketh … account of* to `λογίζεται` headed on *account* and a bare *evil* to `κακόν`, the article standing `unrepresented` under rule 23 as it would in any event. Rule 27 is what forces that, the supplied *account* being what licenses the *of*, and rule 106's accusative arm says the same from the other side: an accusative has no case for an English preposition to realize, so a preposition standing over an accusative object is the verb's or the frame's and never the object's. A genitive or a dative is the contrast and is this rule's ordinary case, its own case being what the English preposition answers to, which is why `τῶν ἀνθρώπων` → *of men* and `τῇ ἀληθείᾳ` → *with the truth* are decided here and not there.
amendments.why: 1CO.13.5 met the case rule 21 had not considered. The rule's sentence 'the case preposition stays with the noun' was written for a genitive or dative, where the English preposition answers to the governed word's case, and a verse pass reading it applied it to an accusative object whose *of* was supplied by the English frame *taketh account of*. The qualification belongs in rule 21 because rule 21 is the rule that was misread: rule 106 already decides the same question, but it opens as a rule about preverbs and no one aligning `λογίζομαι` would look there. Corroborated by rule 106's own accusative arm and its ACT.17 examples (*waited for them*, *feel after him*, *heard of the resurrection*), and by rule 27's refusal to split a helper from what licenses it. Nothing in the corpus queries supplied here contradicts it: every `of the` and `of` unit in the ὁ and ἐκ tables carries a genitive or an expressed preposition, which the amendment leaves exactly as it was.

conventions: An English preposition standing over a governed word belongs to that word only where it realizes the word's own case. Where the ASV builds a support-verb frame around the Greek verb and the frame's supplied noun is what licenses the preposition, the preposition stays inside the verb's unit and the governed word stands bare: 13.5 `οὐ λογίζεται τὸ κακόν` → *taketh not account of evil* gives *taketh … account of* to `λογίζεται` and a bare *evil* to `κακόν`, the accusative having no case for the *of* to answer to. The genitives of 13.1 (*of men*, *of angels*) and 13.13 (*of these*) are the contrast and are rule 21's ordinary case.

Supplied English divides in this chapter by construction and not by the ASV's italics. A word or phrase completing the English expression of one source token is folded onto that token as a rule 7 helper — 13.2 *the gift of* on `προφητείαν`, 13.3 *the poor* on `ψωμίσω`, 13.8 *there be* on each of the three predicate nouns under rules 68 and 96 — while a juncture at an asyndetic seam between two like constituents is `added` under rule 98, as 13.4's *and* between `μακροθυμεῖ` and `χρηστεύεται` is. Both 13.3 and 13.4 name the competing status in their own notes. The cross-verse candidate table is keyed by source lemma and can never show an `added` unit, so this line is recorded here rather than left to be rediscovered from the dump.

report: Cross-verse candidates: all 18 groups checked, none is a split. Every treatment difference is licensed by the ASV's own wording — ὁ is `unrepresented` wherever the ASV writes the noun bare (13.1 *of men* and *of angels*, 13.2 *all mysteries*/*all knowledge*/*all faith*, 13.4/13.8/13.13 bare *love*, 13.6 *in unrighteousness*) and `aligned` wherever it writes a determiner (13.1 and 13.6 *with the*, 13.10 *that which*, 13.11 *things*), which is rule 21 against rule 23, and 13.6 writes both in one verse.

δέ is *but* except where the ASV writes *and* (13.13); καί is *and* except 13.12's *also*, which is rule 82's *also* arm and correctly leaves *even as* whole on καθώς; ἔχω carries a subject pronoun only where the ASV writes one; καταργέω heads on the verb word in all four units (*done away* ×3, *put away*); ὅτε is *When* and *now that*, each the word introducing its English clause; ἐκ μέρους is split token-by-token in all three occurrences under rule 94, while ἐν αἰνίγματι → *darkly* is `noncompositional` by that same single-word test. Nothing in the source licenses a different analysis in any of these.

The candidate table is keyed by source lemma and so is blind to `added` units, so I read the supplied English separately end to end. The chapter folds a supplied completion onto the one token whose English it completes (13.2 *the gift of* on προφητείαν, 13.3 *the poor* on ψωμίσω, 13.8 *there be* ×3 on the predicate nouns) and marks `added` only a juncture at an asyndetic seam between two like finite verbs (13.4 *and*). Those are different constructions — rules 7 and 103 against rule 98 — so this is not a split. Recorded as a convention, since no mechanical table can show it.

One genuine error, patched: 1CO.13.5 `οὐ λογίζεται τὸ κακόν` → *taketh not account of evil* gave *of* to `κακόν` as an *of + noun* rendering under rules 17 and 21. `τὸ κακόν` is accusative, so no case stands for that *of* to realize; the supplied support noun *account* is what licenses it, and rule 27 keeps a helper with what licenses it. Rule 106's accusative arm says the same from the other side, `ἀκούσαντες ἀνάστασιν` → *heard of the resurrection* giving *heard of* to the participle. The patch moves t016 into the `λογίζεται` unit and leaves `κακόν` a bare *evil*; heads are unchanged (*account*, *evil*) and `τό` stays `unrepresented` under rule 23 either way. This also settles an inconsistency inside 13.5 itself, which kept the whole frame *doth behave itself unseemly* inside `ἀσχημονεῖ` two clauses earlier.

BSB disagreements: neither is an error. 13.5 τὰ (`τὰ ἑαυτῆς` → *its own*) is `unrepresented` because the free reflexive genitive takes the possessive and displaces the article's determiner (rule 20), the ASV writing no *things*; the patch does not touch it. 13.11 τοῦ (`τὰ τοῦ νηπίου` → *childish things*) is `unrepresented` because the ASV writes *childish* with no determiner of its own (rule 23), the nominal *things* having gone to the outer article under rule 22. Both are the documented article convention difference, and I changed no accepted edge on their account.

One hard call left standing as the verse pass took it, and it is already noted in its unit: 13.13 gives the written *the* of *the greatest* to the anarthrous `μείζων` under rules 51 and 58 and leaves `ἡ` before `ἀγάπη` `unrepresented`, the copula going to the predicate adjective under rule 63. Handing that *the* to the article across the inversion remains defensible and the unit says so.
